content: Give me a quick list of current inventory.
Sure. I will check the full inventory and share a short summary with SKU, name, and quantity.
Show me all the stock we have today.
Perfect. I will review the current full inventory and show you all available stock.
How much chorizo do we have?
I will search inventory for chorizo and tell you the exact available quantity if I find a single match.
Please show all inventory items before we create an order.
Sure. I will show you the full inventory first; then, if you want, we can build the order.
Create an order with 6 pepino and 4 frijoles.
Done. I will search for those products by name and create the order with the requested quantities when I find a single match for each one.
Also add 2 chayote to the order.
Perfect. I will search for chayote by name and, if there is a single match, add 2 to the latest order.
Change the clamato to 6 on the order.
Sure. I will search for clamato by name and, if it is on the latest order, change that line so the final quantity is 6.
Remove the tostadas from the order.
Understood. I will search for tostadas by name and, if they are on the latest order, remove them from the order.
Please add five of salsa to the order.
Sure. I will search for salsa by name and, if there is a single match, automatically use its SKU to add 5 to the latest order.
Create an order with three chicharron.
Sure. I will search for chicharron by name and, if there is a single match, create the order with 3 units using its SKU automatically.
Put in an order for 4 clamato.
Sure. I will search for clamato by name; if I find a single match, I will use that product and tell you the name, SKU, and order quantity.
Order a dozen tortillas and 6 salsa verde.
Perfect. I will search for tortillas and salsa verde by name, use the SKUs found automatically, and keep the quantities you gave: 12 tortillas and 6 salsa verde.
We received five boxes of chicharron.
Understood. I will search for chicharron by name and record the receipt of 5 boxes if I find a single match.
We sold 2 pepino and three frijoles.
Done. I will search for the products by name and record the sale using the quantities you gave: 2 pepino and 3 frijoles.
Add chicharron and 4 salsa roja to the order.
I can add 4 salsa roja, but I need a quantity for chicharron. How many units do you want to add?
Add 3 mango to the order.
Sure. I will search for mango as a product name and, if I find a single match, add 3 to the order without asking you to confirm the SKU.
I need to order 8 tortillas.
Perfect. I will search inventory for tortillas; if a single product appears, I will use its SKU automatically and create the order with 8 units.
Order 5 salsa.
I will search inventory for salsa. If there are multiple salsas, I will ask you to choose one; if there is only one, I will use its SKU and order 5.
We received 7 tostadas.
Understood. I will search for tostadas by name and, if there is a single match, record the receipt of 7 without asking you to confirm the SKU.
We sold 2 queso.
I will search inventory for queso. If I find multiple queso products, I will ask you to choose the correct product; if there is only one, I will record the sale of 2.
Add 4 salsa to the order.
I can do that, but if the search returns multiple salsa options, I need you to choose the correct product by name. Which salsa do you want to add?
I want to see inventory and also create an order. What should we do first?
To avoid mistakes, I will show you the full inventory first and then create the order. Does that work?
